text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — the docs CI is failing on the SDK examples page after the last PR. build log shows 'fragment not found' for the snippet anchor.
Maya Patel: I saw that when I ran the site locally. The section id got normalized because of an inline code fence.
Jordan Li: Which file? I can take a look.
Alex Chen: docs/reference/sdk/async-client.md — PR #2456. Repro is in the dev build: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/3456
docs-bot: [CI] Build failed — docs/reference/sdk/async-client.md: anchor mismatch (line 124) :warning:
Maya Patel: Minimal repro: we have a fenced code block that contains triple backticks inside a string, e.g. \"```\", and the slugifier ends up stripping differently between dev and prod.
Jordan Li: Ah yeah, nested backticks inside an example string. Docusaurus/mdx slug rules differ from mkdocs in our pipeline.
Sam DevEx: Quick idea — replace the inner triple-backticks with a placeholder and render with a <pre> or use indentation-style code block in that example. That avoids altering heading slugs.
Alex Chen: Patch suggestion posted to PR — changed the example to use indented block and added an explicit heading id: `### Usage {#async-client-usage}`. Also added a small note to the migration guide about escaping backticks in examples.
Maya Patel: Nice. Can you also add a one-line test to docs-build-checker that asserts the generated slug exists in the site output? Prevents regressions.
Jordan Li: On it. I'll add a grep in the e2e script for `async-client-usage` and fail build if missing.
Alex Chen: Updated PR with the changes and test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2456 — PTAL.
Maya Patel: Reviewed + left one nit about wording in the migration guide. :thumbsup:
Jordan Li: Merged the test change to the feature branch. CI rerun queued.
docs-bot: [CI] Build passed — all docs pages generated (after PR patch) :tada:
Alex Chen: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a short note in the docs-tooltips channel about the backtick edge case and the workaround.
Sam DevEx: Can we also add a lint rule to warn on triple-backticks inside string literals in mdx? low-priority but helpful.
Maya Patel: Filed a small task in the docs backlog: DOCS-98 \"MDX inner-backtick lint rule\".
Alex Chen: Great — closing this thread.
